Course Objectives 
The specific objectives of the course are:
1. Understanding some of the basic concepts and theories 
in the field of organizational behavior
2. Examining how individual, group and structural 
variables interact to create knowledge for prediction 
and control
3. Appreciate the implication of concepts and theories in 
the context of Indian situations and research

Basic Concepts
 Organization-A consciously coordinated social
unit, composed of two or more people, that
functions on a relatively continuous basis to
achieve a common goal or sets of goal.
 Behavior is an action or a reaction caused by
either known or unknown stimuli.

BUREAUCRACY
 A component of formal organization that uses rules and 
hierarchical ranking to achieve efficiency
 Ideal type-A construct or model for evaluating specific 
cases
 Ideal bureaucracy displays five basic characteristics: division 
of labor, hierarchy of authority, written rules and regulations, 
impersonality, and employment based on technical 
qualifications

Hierarchy of Authority
 Each position is under the supervision of a higher 
authority
 Such relations can be traced by identifying who 
is answerable to whom

Division of Labor
 Specialized experts perform specific tasks
 Leads to fragmentation of work and isolates workers from 
one another
 Leads to alienation. Alienation-Loss of control over our 
creative human capacity to produce, separation from the 
products we make, and isolation from our fellow producers
 Lessens job security
 Relative isolation makes us unable to recognize our links with 
others. Trained incapacity-The tendency of workers in a 
bureaucracy to become so specialized that they develop 
blind spots and fail to notice potential problems

Written Rules and Regulations
 Through written rules and regulations, bureaucracies 
emphasize clear standards for an adequate performance
 Rules are instrumental for the continuity of the organization
 Overemphasis on rules can lead to goal displacement. Goal 
displacement-Over-zealous conformity to official regulations 
of a bureaucracy

Impersonality
 Bureaucratic officials perform their duties without giving 
personal consideration to people as individuals
 Often contributes to a feeling of frustration and disaffection

Employment Based on 
Technical Qualifications
 Hiring is based on technical qualifications rather 
than on favoritism, and performance is measured 
against specific standards
 Yet dysfunctionality exists within bureaucracy
 Peter principle-A principle of organizational life 
according to which every employee within a 
hierarchy tends to rise to his or her level of 
incompetence

Scientific Management 
Approach
 Proposed by F.W. Taylor and advocated working 
in systematic manner.
 Scientific Management Involved:
The scientific analysis by management of all tasks 
which need to be done for maximum efficiency
Designing jobs by managers to achieve the 
maximum technical division of labor through 
advanced job fragmentation. It involves division 
of labor to allow for separation of tasks and 
functions

Use of incentive payment systems, both to
